Date September 21, 19 32.

Subject (in full) Re Entry Morning State of 21-9-32:- Goods of Japanes Goods
Stolen.

Made by xxx and Forwarded by Inspector Bishop.

Sir,
I beg to report that the accused appeared before the S.S.D.
Court on 21-9-32 when they were each sentenced to 8 months impri-
sonment for snatching.
Complainant was further questioned regarding the incident and
he now alters his statement regarding the route taken with the
goods. He now states that the party proceeded South along North
Chengtu Road to Bubbling Well Road corner, where about 30 or 40
loafers gathered shouting "Japanese Goods." This crowd of loafers
were dispersed by P/S. 282 Makovetsky and C.P.S. 1328, who arrived
on the scene. Complainant's party then crossed Bubbling Well Road
South along Chengtu Road and turned East along Weihaiwei Road.
P/S. 282 and C.P.C. 1328, who were following at a distance, lost
sight of them at this point, and complainant's party then turned
South on Mohawk Road. At Mohawk and Taku Roads corner a crowd of
about 60 loafers gathered and stole the goods.
P/s. 282 Makovetsky and C.P.S. 1328 afterwards saw 2 men carry-
ing a roll of cloth each at Avenue Foch and Tamsui Road corner and
arrested them. Complainant's excuse for giving the wrong route,
when questioned, was that he would not remember which way he went.
The reason that C.P.Cs. and S.P.Cs. en route did not report the
occurrance to the station was because P/S. 282 Makovetsky and CPS.
1328 were escorting the goods when passing their posts and they did
not think there would be any trouble, the crowd who stole the goods
did not really gather until Taku Road was reached.
P/S. 282 Makovetsky did very good work in arresting the four
accused, but neglected to keep up with the trolley and goods he
was escorting and not informing the station or asking for assist-
ance from police en route.
I am, Sir
Your obedient servant,
C. Bishop
Insp. 1/c.

D.O. "B"

由 xxx 制作，由毕晓普（Bishop）督察转送。

先生，
谨此报告，被告于1932年9月21日出庭受审于特区地方法院（S.S.D. Court），每人因抢夺罪被判处8个月监禁。
投诉人就事件接受了进一步讯问，他现在改变了关于货物运送路线的陈述。他现在称，一行人沿成都北路向南行至静安寺路拐角，那里聚集了约30或40名游民，高喊“日本货”。巡长 282 马科夫斯基和华捕 1328 到达现场后驱散了这群游民。投诉人一行人随后穿过静安寺路，沿成都路向南，再沿威海卫路向东。跟随在后方的巡长 282 和华捕头目 1328 在此处失去了他们的踪迹，投诉人一行人随后在莫霍克路（Mohawk Road，注：疑为大沽路Taku Rd之误或特定路段称呼）向南转弯。在大沽路和莫霍克路拐角处，聚集了约60名游民并抢走了货物。
巡长 282 马科夫斯基和华捕 1328 后来在福煦路和淡水路拐角处看到两名男子各扛着一卷布匹，并逮捕了他们。当被问及为何提供错误路线时，投诉人的借口是他记不清走的是哪条路。
沿途的华捕头目和华捕未向捕房报告此事的原因是，当巡长 282 马科夫斯基和华捕 1328 护送货物经过他们的岗位时，他们认为不会有任何麻烦，抢劫货物的人群直到到达大沽路才真正聚集起来。
巡长 282 马科夫斯基在逮捕四名被告方面工作非常出色，但疏忽了跟上他所护送的手推车和货物，也未通知捕房或请求沿途警察协助。
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
C. 毕晓普（Bishop）
主管督察。

“B”区办公室

Sir,

Further enquiries into this case reveal that the four bales
of piece goods and the hand trolley belong to Yang Koh Kao (楊克家)
Piece Goods Merchant, No. 707 North Chengtu Road.

Two coolies named Kong Gee Kwung (江錢坤) and Yang Ching

to Frenchtown via Yates Road, at about 8.30 p.m. on 20-9-32, when

the contents, saying they were Japanese goods.

The two coolies became alarmed and ran away, leaving

Subject (in full) Goods of Japanese Manufacture found abandoned on Yates Road.

Made by D.S. 72 Wilcox. Forwarded by Inspector C. Rishworth

Sir,
At about 8.30p.m. on 20-9-32, P.S. 148 Aston, was on b/cycle patrol proceeding South along Yates Road when he observed about 100 persons assembled on the East side of the road, about 200 yards south of Bubbling Well Road. He immediately proceeded to the scene and discovered that several of the crowd were tampering 4 bales of piece goods, which were loaded on a handtrolley at the side of the road.
The crowd dispersed on his arrival. Enquiries revealed that the four bales contained rolls of cotton cloth manufactured by the Dong Shing (Japanese) Spinning and Weaving Co. Ltd. and that the coolie who was drawing the trolley, had run away after having been attacked by some unknown Chinese.
Enquiries were made in the vicinity, but no clue to the owner of the goods could be found.
The goods have been removed to this Station and efforts are being made to locate the owner.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

DISTURBANCE OVER TRANSPORTATION OF JAPANESE GOODS.

At 7.50 p.m., 10-9-32, a telephone message was received at this Station from C.P.C.2927 to the effect that a crowd is holding up some Japanese goods on Fokien Road near Peking Road. A party of Police immediately attended. On arrival of Police two hand trollies loaded with 8 bales of Japanese cloth, were found left unattended at the above corner and the crowd disappeared. The bales were removed to the Station for safety in the Police riding van. From enquiries made by C.D.C.132 and the undersigned the following was ascertained: Zih Yeu Sao (席興泰) shop-keeper of An Zung Yuen (衡盛元) Piece Goods Shop, 46 South Wusih Road ordered his two coolies to remove the above property to Yoeng Tai Ziang (永泰祥) Shop, 73-4 Kwangse Road. Some unknown coolies on seeing the coolies transporting the Japanese goods interfered and a crowd collected, examining the goods, when the two coolies in charge ran away. The above named shop-master came to the Station and the property was returned to him at 9.30 p.m. even date which he removed on a motor truck to the above mentioned place, where he was sending it when the trouble occurred.

The above named master admitted that the goods were of Japanese manufacturing and a Police escort was detailed to escort the goods to the place of destination.

先生，
1932年8月22日晚上9时35分，第55分局警长 Wilkinson 致电本分局，称在法租界爱德华七世路附近的格罗男爵路（Rue Baron Gros），有抵制者扣留了日货。当时无外籍警探可用（警探副督察 Wilcox 和本人均外出办案），菲利普斯督察偕同华捕第265号和第189号，陪同日本领事馆警探第4号渡边（H）及日本领事馆警探前往霞飞路分局，经查实，由神户矢野商会（H. Yano & Co, Kobe）出口至南京路70号南本洋行（Minamimoto Yoko）的日货，包括5箱价值320.00美元的自行车配件，正被运往江西路的一家中国商店（姓名和地址未透露）。约于1932年8月22日晚上8时到达江西路与爱德华七世路路口时，搬运货物的苦力被三名中国人拦下，其中一人骑自行车，并被迫将装有箱子的手推车沿爱德华七世路向西推行。南本洋行通知了日本领事馆警察，日本领事馆警探第4号渡边随同他们沿爱德华七世路前行。货物在爱德华七世路与格罗男爵路路口被发现。晚上9时30分，一名骑自行车的中国人在爱德华七世路与莫霍克路（Mohawk Road）转角处被华捕第851号拦下。该华捕称，此人最初告诉他，有一辆载有几个箱子的手推车被弃置在爱德华七世路与格罗男爵路路口无人看管。该华捕将其指引至法国巡捕房，此人便去通知法国巡捕房，但后来在日本人的唆使下又被拦下。货物由法国巡捕房接管，新闸分局在晚上9时37分通过电话获悉此事后，一旦收到事件信息即采取行动。华捕第851号于晚上9时30分左右逮捕的男子是姚宗泰（Yao Zung Tai），20岁，宁波人，未婚，福州路444号伟通电气公司（Wei Tong Electric Co.）学徒。

Special Branch S. I. Station,
Date 17 / 8 / 32
Date August 16, 1932.

Subject (in full)...... Chinese Press Report of Alleged Japanese
goods seized in Chinese City - attached press report.
Made by...... D.I. Sih Tse-liang ......Forwarded by JHP Robertson, Supt

Discreet enquiries along Kin Kuo Road, in the
vicinity of Old North Gate elicit the information that
at 8.40 p.m. August 8, 1932 about forty Chinese surrounded
a handcart loaded with 2 wooden boxes which it was alleged
contained goods of Japanese make. While the crowd
offered suggestions as to ways to deal with the goods,
the Chinese constable on post duty at the entrance to the
Old North Gate, City, approached and in order to avoid
possible disorder and congestion of traffic, took the
handcart and the goods to the 1st Sub-Station, 2nd District.
Meanwhile, a Chinese who gave his name as Chu Chao-peng
(詹兆本) and claimed to have followed the goods from
the French Concession, volunteered to go to the Station
to offer an explanation as to the origin of the goods.
He accordingly accompanied the goods to the Public Safety
Bureau, where he departed after having given his name and
address. The goods in question are still detained in
the Bureau pending the turning up of their owner.

Sih Tse Liang
D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
Ob. (borne)
Information
J. L. Evans
O. i/c Sp. Br.

在老北门附近的金国路（Kin Kuo Road）一带进行谨慎查访后获悉，1932年8月8日晚上8时40分，约四十名中国人包围了一辆装载2个木箱的手推车，据称箱内装有日本制造的商品。当人群就如何处理这些货物提出建议时，驻守老城老北门入口处的华捕上前，为了避免可能发生的混乱和交通拥堵，将手推车和货物带至第二区第一分所。与此同时，一名自称朱兆鹏（Chu Chao-peng，原文注：詹兆本）的中国人声称从法租界一路跟随货物而来，自愿前往分局解释货物的来源。他随即陪同货物前往公安局，在留下姓名和地址后离开。上述货物仍扣押在局内，等待物主出现。

Sih Tse Liang

August 8, 1932. Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:

THE BOYCOTT MOVEMENT : THREATS TO MERCHANTS.

On August 6, the Coal Merchants Association again received a letter of warning from the Blood & Soul Corps for the Extermination of Traitors. The letter threatened to bomb every traitorous merchants in case they continue in their foolish policy.
In consequence of this, there was a rumour that the Blood & Soul Corps for the Extermination of Traitors would bomb the Coal Quotations Room yesterday. The Louza Station yesterday detailed detectives and policemen to the premises of the Association to maintain precautionary measures. However, no untoward incident happened.
The coal quotations room closed an hour earlier yesterday.

&
A few days ago, the Rubber Metal and- Supplies Merchants Association received a letter of warning from the Blood & Soul Corps for the Extermination of Traitors.
The Association held a meeting at 3 p.m. yesterday when it was resolved to notify all its members not to deal in Japanese goods and to organise an Investigation Group to carry out inspection work.

The Japanese Goods Inspection Section of the Restaurant Merchants Association has issued a circular notice to all its members informing them not to purchase enemy goods.

The Fish Merchants Association has decided at a meeting held recently to urge all its members to organise Secret Investigation Groups for the purpose of ascertaining whether any traders are dealing in enemy goods.

Chen Pao:

Arrest of a Member of National Salvation Ten-Men Group.

On the night of August 6, Chinese Police arrested a man named Chu Zau Pang on Min Kuo Road, Nantao, who with others attempted to set fire to two boxes of enemy cotton on a small barrow. Chu was immediately taken to the 1st Division of the 2nd District Police Station. When questioned, he stated that he was a member of the National Salvation Ten-Men Group.
Chu was then removed to the Headquarters of the Public Safety Bureau.

1932年8月8日。下午译文。

杂项

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

抵制运动：对商人的威胁。

8月6日，煤炭同业公会再次收到“诛奸灭魂团”的警告信。信中威胁说，如果奸商继续其愚蠢政策，将对每一位奸商实施炸弹袭击。
因此，有谣言称“诛奸灭魂团”将于昨日轰炸煤炭报价所。老闸分局昨日派遣警探和警察前往公会所在地采取预防措施。然而，未发生任何意外事件。
昨日煤炭报价所提前一小时关门。

&

数日前，橡胶金属及用品同业公会收到“诛奸灭魂团”的警告信。
该公会于昨日下午3时召开会议，决议通知所有会员不得经营日货，并组织调查组开展检查工作。

餐饮业同业公会的日货检查科已向所有会员发出通函，告知他们不得购买敌货。

鱼业同业公会在最近举行的会议上决定，敦促所有会员组织秘密调查组，以查明是否有商人经营敌货。

《晨报》：

逮捕一名“救国十人团”成员。

8月6日晚，中国警察在南市民国路逮捕了一名名为朱佐邦（Chu Zau Pang）的男子，他与他人试图点燃小推车上两箱敌产棉花。朱随即被带至第二区警察总局第一科。经讯问，他声称自己是“救国十人团”成员。
朱随后被移送至公安局总部。

April 16, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

MAINICHI

ARIYOSHI REQUESTS WANG CHING WEI TO SUPPRESS
ANTI-JAPANESE ACTIVITIES

A telegram from Nanking
reports that on April 15 Mr. Ariyoshi, Japanese Minister
to China, in company with secretaries Horiuchi and
Arino, called on Wang Ching Wei and requested him to
suppress the anti-Japanese activities effectively
because, according to reports submitted at the conference
of Japanese Consuls-General held recently, such activities
were still going on although he appreciated the sincerity
of the Chinese authorities in their desire to suppress
them.

In reply, Mr. Wang Ching
Wei promised to do his utmost.
Views were then exchanged on
the regulations governing the marking of the place of origin
on imported goods.

Afterwards Mr. Ariyoshi
informed newspaper reporters that he had come to Nanking
to bid farewell to Mr. Wang Ching Wei as he was leaving
China for Japan on April 20 on the S.S. Tatsuta Maru.
As regards the suppression of anti-Japanese activities,
the Chinese government was doing its best but the work was,
so far, not satisfactory. Therefore, Wang Ching Wei
had been requested to bring about an effective suppression.
Mr. Ariyoshi will attend a
party to be given in his honor by Wang Ching Wei on the
evening of April 15. He will invite Wang Ching Wei
to a dinner at the Japanese Consulate-General in Nanking.

NICHI-NICHI

JAPANESE MONTHLY MAGAZINE ENTITLED "GREAT SHANGHAI"
TO APPEAR IN MAY

Holding the view that an
ideal publication was needed in Shanghai to lead the
thirty thousand Japanese residents, Mr. J. Togo, an
artist by profession, who lives in the premises of the
Shanghai Mainichi Shimbun, will publish in May a monthly
magazine to be called "Great Shanghai".
The aim of the magazine is
to point out how unhealthy is the spirit of the Japanese
community in Shanghai and how inadequate is their knowledge
of public affairs.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER APR 18 1935 CRIME BRANCH）

1935年4月16日。下午译文。

《每日新闻》

有吉明请求汪精卫镇压反日活动

来自南京的电讯报道，4月15日，日本驻华公使有吉明先生在秘书堀内和荒野的陪同下，拜访了汪精卫，请求他有效镇压反日活动，因为根据最近在日本总领事会议上提交的报告，尽管他赞赏中国当局镇压反日活动的诚意，但此类活动仍在继续。

作为回应，汪精卫先生承诺将竭尽全力。
随后，双方就进口商品产地标记的规定交换了意见。

此后，有吉明先生告知新闻记者，他来到南京是为了向汪精卫先生辞行，因为他将于4月20日乘坐“龙田丸”号轮船离开中国前往日本。关于镇压反日活动，中国政府正在尽力而为，但迄今为止工作并不令人满意。因此，已请求汪精卫实现有效镇压。有吉明先生将出席汪精卫于4月15日晚为他举行的宴会。他将邀请汪精卫参加在南京日本总领事馆举行的晚宴。

《日日新闻》

题为《大上海》的日本月刊将于五月出版

持有一种观点认为，上海需要一份理想的刊物来引导三万日本居民，居住在上海《每日新闻》报社内的职业艺术家东乡（J. Togo）先生，将于五月出版一本名为《大上海》的月刊。
该杂志的宗旨是指出上海日本侨民社会的精神状态多么不健康，以及他们对公共事务的了解多么不足。

（印：副总监 1935年4月18日 刑侦处）

April 15, 1935. Morning Translation

NICHI-NICHI

MR. ARIYOSHI REPORTS TO FOREIGN OFFICE ON THE
ANTI-JAPANESE ACTIVITIES IN CHINA

A Dentsu telegram from
Tokyo dated April 14 reports that the conference of
all Japanese Consuls-General in China would have an
important bearing in determining Japan's China policy.
At the conference which was held in Shanghai the
Consuls-General submitted reports on anti-Japanese
activities, the instructions of the Chinese Government
regarding the suppression of anti-Japanese activities
and the results of the suppression in their respective
areas. Views were exchanged regarding the policy to
be adopted.

On April 13 the Foreign
Office received the following report from the Japanese
Minister to China regarding the situation relating to
the suppression of anti-Japanese activities in China:-
1. In the North the anti-Japanese movement has
never been active so that no noticeable change in regard
to the anti-Japanese movement is apparent.
2. In the places along the Yangtsze valley, in
Tientsin and in Fukien province the situation of anti-
Japanese activities has become easier than before.
3. In Shanghai the anti-Japanese resolutions
adopted by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the
various merchants guilds have so far not been cancelled
and transactions in Japanese goods are not fully recovered.
The economic depression in China may be partly responsible
for the lifeless stat. of business.
4. In South-West China anti-Japanese movement is
still carried on strongly although the cause may be
attributed to the political estrangement of the Nanking
and the Canton Governments.

ARRIVAL OF JAPANESE NOTABLES

and Count Hotta, Vice Minister
of the Navy, Major-General Ishotani, newly appointed
Military Attache to the Japanese Legation, arrived in
Shanghai at 4.30 p.m. April 14 on the S.S. Nagasaki
Maru. They were received at the Wayside Wharf by
a number of Japanese high officials.

NIPPO

ARIYOSHI TO LEAVE FOR NANKING TO-DAY

It is reported that Mr.
Ariyoshi, Japanese Minister to China, was to leave for
Nanking yesterday but he will leave to-day instead.

《日日新闻》

有吉明就中国反日活动向外务省报告

东京4月14日电通社电讯报道，在华所有日本总领事会议将对确定日本对华政策产生重要影响。在上海举行的会议上，各总领事提交了关于反日活动、中国政府关于镇压反日活动的指示以及各自辖区镇压结果的报告。双方就拟采取的政策交换了意见。

4月13日，外务省收到日本驻华公使关于中国镇压反日活动情况的以下报告：-
1. 在北方，反日运动一直不活跃，因此反日运动方面没有明显变化。
2. 在长江流域各地、天津和福建省，反日活动的局势比以前有所缓和。
3. 在上海，中国总商会和各商人公会通过的反日决议迄今尚未取消，日货交易也未完全恢复。中国的经济萧条可能是造成商业低迷的部分原因。
4. 在中国西南，反日运动仍然强烈进行，尽管其原因可归咎于南京政府与广州政府之间的政治疏远。

日本要人抵达

海军次官堀田伯爵、新任日本公使馆武官石谷少将，于4月14日下午4时30分乘坐“长崎丸”号抵达上海。他们在码头栈桥受到多位日本高官的接待。

有吉明今日启程赴南京

据报道，日本驻华公使有吉明先生原计划昨日启程赴南京，但他将改为今日启程。

April 13, 1935. Morning Translation.

NIPPO

MR. FUNATSU AND MR. OKAMOTO TO BE ENTERTAINED BY
PROMINENT JAPANESE RESIDENTS

It is reported that a number
of prominent Japanese residents, including Mr. Ishii,
Consul-General, Mr. Yonegato, Chairman of the Japanese
Chamber of Commerce, and Mr. Sugimoto, acting Chairman
of the Japanese Residents Corporation, will entertain
Mr. Funatsu and Mr. Okamoto who had served on the S.M.C.
as the representatives of the Japanese Community for
many years.
The function will take place
at the Japanese Club at noon April 19.

D.3/ent. ADMIRAL HYAKUTAKE TO GIVE TEA PARTY

Rear-Admiral Hyakutake,
Commander-in-Chief of the Third Fleet, will give a tea
party to a number of prominent persons at the headquarters
of the Japanese Landing Party at 4 p.m. April 14. Count
Hotta, Vice Minister of the Navy, will attend the party. X

MR. YADA ARRIVES IN SHANGHAI

Mr. Yada, former Consul-General
at Shanghai now State Councillor to Manchukuo, arrived
in Shanghai at 9.30 a.m. April 12. He is staying at the
Astor House.

D3753. JAPANESE LODGE COMPLAINT WITH FRENCH AND CHINESE
AUTHORITIES REGARDING TWO SINO-JAPANESE WAR PICTURES
FOUND IN FRENCH CONCESSION

It is reported that two Sino-
Japanese war pictures, the character of which is liable
to create ill feeling between Japanese and Chinese, are
being displayed at the Sun Ho Tei Fruit Shop and at the
Hung Shing Department Store on Rue du Consulate, French
Concession.
S Holding the view that the
exhibition of such pictures is liable to be harmful to
Sino-Japanese rapprochement, the Japanese Consular authorities
will lodge a protest with the French and Chinese authorities
and will request that the exhibition of such pictures
be prohibited.

1935年4月13日。晨间译件。

《日本新闻》（NIPPO）

 prominent Japanese residents 将宴请船津先生和冈本先生

据报，包括石井总领事、日本商会会长米内户先生、以及日本居留民团代理理事长杉本先生在内的一批知名日侨，将宴请曾在工部局担任日方代表多年的船津先生和冈本先生。
该活动将于4月19日中午在日本俱乐部举行。

D.3/ent. 百武少将将举办茶话会

第三舰队司令长官百武少将将于4月14日下午4时，在日本海军陆战队司令部为一批知名人士举办茶话会。海军次官堀田伯爵将出席该茶话会。X

矢田先生抵达上海

前驻上海总领事、现伪满洲国国务顾问矢田先生，于4月12日上午9时30分抵达上海。他下榻于汇中饭店（Astor House）。

D3753. 日本领馆就法租界发现的两幅中日战争图片向法国及中国当局提出交涉

据报，在法租界领事馆路（Rue du Consulate）的孙和泰水果店和鸿兴百货公司，正在展出两幅性质容易引发日中之间恶感的中日战争图片。
鉴于此类图片的展示有碍日中和睦，日本领事当局将向法国及中国当局提出抗议，并要求禁止展示此类图片。

April 4, 1935. Morning Translation. 4. 4. 35.

NICHI-NICHI

BRITISH MINISTER TO MEET JAPANESE MINISTER

The British Minister to
China arrived in Shanghai on April 1. He informed
newspaper reporters that during his visit to Nanking
he paid several calls on the Foreign Minister and
the Finance Minister to discuss the question of a
loan to China but no progress was made and further
conferences were expected.
During his stay in Shanghai,
the British Minister will meet the Japanese Minister
to China to exchange views regarding the loan.

CHIEF OF JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE ENTERTAINS
JAPANESE NEWSPAPER REPORTERS

At 5 p.m. April 3 Mr. Uyeda,
Chief of the Japanese Consular Police, entertained
20 Japanese newspaper reporters, correspondents and
representatives of important Japanese newspapers at
the Lion Cafe, Chapoo Road. A number of officers
of the Japanese Consulate attended.

D 5354
S

THE INCREASE IN THE TELEPHONE RATE

At 4.30 p.m. April 3 a
meeting was held by the Shanghai Municipal Council to
consider the increase in the telephone rate, but no
definite decision was reached. The matter will be
discussed again at another meeting to be held by the
Council before the ratepayers meeting.
It is not certain whether a
final decision will be sought at the ratepayers meeting
or whether the retiring Council will decide the matter
and include its decision in the annual report to be
presented to the ratepayers meeting.

MAINICHI

D 3753
S

CHINA TAKES MEASURES TO SUPPRESS ANTI-JAPANESE
ACTIVITIES

The instructions issued by
the Nanking Government on March 5 to all Kuomintang
Committees and Chambers of Commerce throughout China
to suppress anti-Japanese activities have been well
received by the Chinese people.
On March 12 the Shanghai City Government issued
a notification announcing the sincere intention of the
Nanking Government to suppress anti-Japanese activities
and instructing the public to observe strictly the
regulations governing the suppression of anti-Japanese
activities.
On March 10 the Hopei Provincial Government issued
a notification explaining the instructions issued by
Wang Ching Wei regarding anti-Japanese activities and
ordered the public to observe these instructions.

1935年4月4日。晨间译件。1935年4月4日。

《日日新闻》（NICHI-NICHI）

英国公使将会见日本公使

英国驻华公使于4月1日抵达上海。他告知新闻记者，他在南京访问期间，曾数次拜访外交部长和财政部长，讨论对华贷款问题，但未取得进展，预计还将举行进一步会谈。
在上海停留期间，英国公使将会见日本驻华公使，就贷款问题交换意见。

日本领事警察主任宴请日本报社记者

4月3日下午5时，日本领事警察主任上田先生在乍浦路狮子咖啡馆（Lion Cafe）宴请了20位日本报社记者、通讯员及重要日本报纸的代表。多名日本领事馆官员出席了宴会。

D 5354
S

电话费率上涨

4月3日下午4时30分，上海公共租界工部局召开会议审议电话费率上涨事宜，但未作出明确决定。此事将在纳税人会议之前由工部局召开的另一次会议上再次讨论。
目前尚不确定是在纳税人会议上寻求最终决定，还是由卸任工部局决定此事，并将决定列入提交给纳税人会议的年度报告中。

《每日新闻》（MAINICHI）

D 3753
S

中国采取措施镇压反日活动

南京政府于3月5日向全中国的国民党各委员会和商会发出的镇压反日活动的指令，已受到中国人民的欢迎。
3月12日，上海市政府发布通告，宣布南京政府镇压反日活动的诚意，并指示公众严格遵守有关镇压反日活动的规定。
3月10日，河北省政府发布通告，解释汪精卫关于反日活动的指令，并命令公众遵守这些指令。

April 4, 1935. Morning Translation.

-2-

（批：D 9753 Cancelled）

On March 12 the Bureau of Public Safety in
Shantung Province issued a notification warning the
public not to become involved in any incidents that
are liable to give rise to diplomatic questions. On
March 16 another notification was issued containing
the instructions issued by Wang Ching Wei regarding
anti-Japanese activities and ordering the public to
observe the regulations governing the suppression of
anti-Japanese activities.
In Peiping an official notification was issued
to the effect that instructions to suppress anti-Japanese
activities have been received from the Central Government.
On March 20 the Kiangsi Provincial Government
issued an order in Kiukiang prohibiting an exhibition
of anti-Japanese pictures.

NIPPO

NAVAL MANOEUVRES IN THE EASTERN SEA

A Dentsu telegram from
Sasebo dated April 3 reports that naval manoeuvres
have been started by the 1st and 2nd Fleets in the
Eastern Sea since April 1 and will last until the
morning of April 4.

REAR-ADMIRAL ARAKI TO DELIVER LECTURE ON
ARMAMENT AND DISARMAMENT

Rear-Admiral Araki, Commander
of the Japanese Landing Party, will deliver a lecture
on the subject "Armament and Disarmament" at a meeting
of the Japanese Thursday Society at the Oyu Club at
6.30 p.m. April 4. The lecture is open to the public.

3月12日，山东省公安局发布通告，警告公众不要卷入任何可能引起外交问题的事故。3月16日，又发布另一份通告，其中包含汪精卫关于反日活动的指令，并命令公众遵守有关镇压反日活动的规定。
在北平，官方发布通告称，已收到中央政府关于镇压反日活动的指令。

《日本新闻》（NIPPO）

东海海军演习

据4月3日从佐世保发出的电通社电讯报道，第一和第二舰队自4月1日起在东海开始海军演习，并将持续至4月4日上午。

荒木少将就军备与裁军发表演讲

日本海军陆战队指挥官荒木少将，将于4月4日下午6时30分，在大洋俱乐部（Oyu Club）举行的日本星期四协会会议上，就“军备与裁军”主题发表演讲。该讲座对公众开放。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 3753
Date 3 / 4 / 35

April 3, 1935. Morning Translation.

NIPPO

D3753
S

JAPANESE AUTHORITIES TO LODGE PROTEST AGAINST ANTI-
JAPANESE BROADCASTING

It is reported that a certain
radio station in Shanghai broadcasts an anti-Japanese
programme in the Peking, Shanghai, Shantung and Ningpo
dialects every night between 10.10 and 10.30 o'clock.
to advocate a boycott of Japanese goods and to promote
native products. Abusive words are used to create bad
feeling against Japan.
The Japanese authorities will
lodge an energetic protest with the Shanghai City Government
as soon as the wave length of the broadcasting station
concerned has been ascertained.

JAPANESE AUTHORITIES ANGRY WITH CHINESE DIPLOMATS
FOR THEIR ANTI-JAPANESE ACTIVITIES

Whether they are acting on
the instructions of the Chinese Foreign Office or in
accordance with private feelings, it is a fact that a
number of Chinese diplomats abroad are reported to be
actively engaged in anti-Japanese movements at this time
when Sino-Japanese relations are making good progress.
It is reported that Quo Tai
Chi , Chinese Minister to Great Britain, and Ho Sze Teh,
Chinese Minister to Switzerland, recently delivered
anti-Japanese speeches at the Oxford China Society. The
speeches were later printed and distributed. These two
Chinese diplomats are trying to induce the League of
Nations to engage in anti-Japanese activities and to secure
an international loan without Japanese participation.
The Japanese authorities are
paying serious attention to the activities of these
Chinese diplomats.

NICHI-NICHI

D6501

MAJOR-GENERAL DOIHARA REPORTS TO THE WAR OFFICE

A Dentsu telegram from Tokyo
dated April 2 reports that Major-General
Doihara, Chief of the Special Military Organ in Mukden,
arrived in Tokyo on April 1 and submitted to the War
Office a report on the results of his inspection tour in
China.
The following is a gist of the
report submitted to the War Office:-
"Of late Sino-Japanese relations.
have improved, but the Nanking Government is still adopting
her customary policy of be-friending remote countries and
opposing neighbouring countries because the officials of
the Government are insincerely attempting to restore proper
relations between China and Japan. Japan should not take
any notice of China's gesture but carry out her predetermined
policy. Any proposition made by the Nanking Government
cannot be depended upon so long as the Chinese do not cease
their anti-Japanese activities and their policy of anti-
Japanese education."

1935年4月3日。晨间译件。

《日本新闻》（NIPPO）

D3753
S

日本当局将对反日广播提出抗议

据报，上海某广播电台每晚10点10分至10点30分之间，用北京话、上海话、山东话和宁波话广播反日节目，鼓吹抵制日货并提倡国货。节目中使用了辱骂性言辞以制造对日本的恶感。
一旦查明相关广播电台的波长，日本当局将立即向上海市政府提出强烈抗议。

日本当局对中国外交官的反日活动感到愤怒

无论他们是奉中国外交部之命行事，还是出于个人情感，事实是，据报道，在中日关系取得良好进展的当下，一些驻外中国外交官正积极参与反日运动。
据报，中国驻英公使郭泰祺和中国驻瑞士公使贺世杰，最近在牛津中国学会发表了反日演讲。这些演讲随后被印刷并分发。这两位中国外交官正试图促使国际联盟参与反日活动，并在没有日本参与的情况下获得国际贷款。
日本当局正密切关注这些中国外交官的活动。

《日日新闻》（NICHI-NICHI）

D6501

土肥原少将向陆军省报告

据4月2日从东京发出的电通社电讯报道，沈阳特务机关长土肥原少将于4月1日抵达东京，并向陆军省提交了其在中国视察结果的报告。
以下是提交给陆军省的报告要点：
“近来中日关系有所改善，但南京政府仍采取其惯用的‘远交近攻’政策，因为政府官员并非真诚地试图恢复中日正常关系。日本不应理会中国的姿态，而应执行其既定政策。只要中国人不停止其反日活动和反日教育政策，南京政府提出的任何主张都不可信赖。”

S. S. REGISTRY.

Date 27. 3. 1935.

March 27, 1935. Afternoon translation.

Chinese Authorities Dealing Strictly With Anti-Japanese
Activities

A telegram from Kiukiang reports
that several days ago a Chinese book shop in Kiukiang
exhibited a printed picture of an anti-Japanese character.
On March 24 the Kiangsu Provincial Government issued an order
prohibiting the shop from exhibiting the picture.

This prompt action on the part of
the Chinese authorities should appease the feeling of un-
easiness among Japanese which and been created by the strange
incident which took place at the reception given to the
Japanese goodwill eviators at Nanking.

1935年3月27日。午后译件。

中国当局严厉处理反日活动

来自九江的电讯报道称，几天前，九江一家中国书店展出了一幅具有反日性质的印刷图片。3月24日，江苏省政府发布命令，禁止该店展示该图片。

中国当局的这一迅速行动，应能平息因在南京举行的欢迎日本亲善飞行员招待会上发生的奇怪事件而在日本人中造成的不安情绪。

March 21, 1935. Afternoon translation.

NANKING SEEKS UNDERSTANDING WITH TOKYO REGARDING SUPPRESSION
OF ANTI-JAPANESE BOYSCOTT MOVEMENT

A Rengo telegram from Tokyo
dated March 20 reports that on March 19 the Foreign Office
received a telegram from Mr. Ariyosgi, Japanese Minister
to China, stating that the Nanking Government is seeking
an understanding with the Tokyo Government regarding the
suppression of the anti-Japanese boycott movement in
China Because certain discontented elements are still
engaged in anti-Japanese activities although the anti-
Japanese movement is being suppressed throughout China.

Japanese residents in China
are keeping a close watch on the effect of the orders
issued by the Nanking Government for the suppression
of the anti-Japanese boycott movement and they will
draw the attention the central and local authorities
to the petty activities of anti-Japanese bodies in order
to bring about a complete suppression of such activities.

1935年3月21日。午后译件。

南京就镇压反日抵制运动一事寻求与东京达成谅解

据3月20日从东京发出的联合通讯社电讯报道，3月19日，日本外务省收到日本驻华公使有吉先生的电报，称南京政府正就镇压中国境内的反日抵制运动一事，寻求与东京政府达成谅解，因为尽管全中国都在镇压反日运动，但某些不满分子仍在从事反日活动。

在华日侨正密切关注南京政府发布的镇压反日抵制运动命令的效果，他们将提请中央和地方当局注意反日团体的细微活动，以便彻底镇压此类活动。

March 19, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

NIPPO

ARRIVAL OF GENERAL DOIHARA

Major-General Doihara who has been on a tour of inspection in the South returned to Shanghai on March 18 on the S.S. Chosa Maru. He is staying at the Towa Yoko Hotel.

BRITISH AND AMERICAN MISSIONARIES DISPLAY ANTI-JAPANESE SENTIMENT

Some time ago it was reported that the National Government through the Ministry of Education had issued instructions to all American missionary schools to cease the use of school books containing anti-Japanese propaganda. However, according to reliable sources the report is not true. The National Government is only making investigations into the matter.
It was ascertained that recently British and American missionaries held a joint meeting in Shanghai when they passed a resolution to oppose the policies of Japan.

THE VISIT TO NANKING OF DR. KUNG, CHINESE MINISTER OF FINANCE MAY BE CONNECTED WITH BRITISH MINISTER'S ACTIVITY

Mr. Wang Ching Wei, President of the Executive Yuan, arrived in Shanghai on March 18 and hold a conference with Dr. Kung, Finance Minister, and Mr. T. V. Soong to discuss financial matters.
At 11 p.m. March 18 Mr. Wang Ching Wei and Dr. Kung proceeded to Nanking. The nature of the conference held between the three officials is not known but the Finance Minister's visit to Nanking appears to be related to the activities of British Minister.
the

MAINICHI

GENERAL SUZUKI LEAVES SHANGHAI

Lieutenant-General Suzuki, former Military Attache to the Japanese Legation, left here on March 18 on the S.S. Shanghai Maru to take up his post as commander of the 19th Division at Ranan, Korea.

CHIANG KAI SHEK KEEPS CLOSE WATCH ON CHINESE COOPERATING WITH JAPAN

Following the report that Sino-Japanese relations had improved, Chiang Kai Shek, Chairman of the Military Commission, in cooperation with the Kuomintang, is reported to be endeavouring to suppress the anti-Japanese movement, the continuation of which is opposed by Japan.

杂项

《日本新闻》（NIPPO）

土肥原将军抵达

在南方视察的土肥原少将于3月18日乘“朝潮丸”轮（S.S. Chosa Maru）返回上海。他下榻于东亚酒店（Towa Yoko Hotel）。

英美传教士表现出反日情绪

此前曾有报道称，国民政府通过教育部向所有美国教会学校发出指令，停止使用含有反日宣传的教科书。然而，据可靠消息来源，该报道不实。国民政府仅在此事上进行调查。
经查实，近期英美传教士在上海举行联席会议，并通过了一项反对日本政策的决议。

中国财政部长孔祥熙博士访问南京可能与英国公使的活动有关

行政院院长汪精卫先生于3月18日抵达上海，并与财政部长孔祥熙博士及宋子文先生举行会议，讨论财务事宜。
3月18日晚11时，汪精卫先生和孔祥熙博士前往南京。这三位官员之间会议的性质尚不清楚，但财政部长的南京之行似乎与英国公使的活动有关。

《每日新闻》（MAINICHI）

铃木将军离开上海

前日本公使馆武官铃木中将，于3月18日乘“上海丸”轮（S.S. Shanghai Maru）离开此地，赴朝鲜罗南（Ranan）就任第19师团师团长一职。

蒋介石严密监视与日本合作的中国人

据报道，随着中日关系改善的消息传出，军事委员会委员长蒋介石在与国民党合作下，正努力镇压反日运动，因为日本反对该运动的持续。

反日运动——“铁血锄奸团”——活动

浙江北路211号奎安社（Kui An Shee）商店约于一周前收到一封信函，声称发自“铁血锄奸团”，指控该店购买“敌国”来源的皮革。该店经理在1935年3月12日的《新闻报》上刊登广告，驳斥了这一指控。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 3753
Date 13 / 3 / 35

March 13, 1935. Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

NICHI-NICHI

JAPANESE SEA PRODUCTS SEIZED BY CHINESE AT HANGCHOW

Following the proposal for
Sino-Japanese economic co-operation the anti-Japanese
movement of the Chinese appeared to show signs of having
quietened down. We learn, however, that there are still
those who wish to carry on the movement. Japanese
sugar, sea products and paper are the principal products
which have been boycotted by the Chinese.
It is reported that a quantity
of Japanese sea weed valued at about $2,000 which was
sold by a Japanese firm in Shanghai to a Chinese merchant
was seized at Hangchow by an anti-Japanese organization.
The Japanese firm is reported to be negotiating with
the anti-Japanese organization for the release of the
goods.
Hangchow is a place where
the people consume a great deal of Japanese sea foods,
nevertheless, the anti-Japanese boycott movement is
still active and the seizure of Japanese goods purchased
by Chinese merchants still goes on.

MAINICHI

EDITOR OF THE OBSERVER URGES BRITISH PUBLIC TO RECOGNIZE
JAPAN'S ANNEXATION OF MANCHUKUO AND INNER
MONGOLIA

A Rengo telegram from London
dated March 11 reports that Mr. Garbin(?) Chief editor
of the Observer, published the following article in his
paper on March 10 in connection with Far Eastern
affairs, in the course of which he urged the public
to recognize the annexation of Manchukuo and Inner
Mongolia:-
"World disarmament will never be realized
unless the Far Eastern problem is solved. It is feared
that there will always be danger as long as the governments
of the Powers cannot adopt a plan to deal with the Far
Eastern question. All the powers including Japan must
agree to a ten year peace plan. In order to bring about
the proposal, one condition must be observed by the Powers,
namely, the annexation of Manchukuo and a part of Inner
Mongolia by Japan. In any consideration of the relations
between Japan and China, Japan's position must be recognized,
geographically and economically. It is not known whether
Japan will insist on preferential rights in China or
whether she will be satisfied with financial guarantees.
The solution of the Far Eastern question is a most difficult
matter but the adoption of a political and constructive
plan would meet the situation."
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部登记处。
编号 D 3753
日期 1935年3月13日

1935年3月13日。晨间译件。

杂项

《日日新闻》

中国人在杭州扣押日本海产品

随着中日经济合作提议的提出，中国人的反日运动似乎呈现出平息迹象。然而，据悉仍有人希望继续该运动。日本糖、海产品和纸张是中国人抵制的主要产品。
据报道，一家日本商社在上海卖给一名中国商人的一批价值约2,000美元的日本海藻，在杭州被一个反日组织扣押。据悉，该日本商社正在与反日组织谈判，要求释放货物。
杭州是一个消费大量日本海产品的地方，尽管如此，反日抵制运动依然活跃，扣押中国商人购买的日本货物的行为仍在继续。

《每日新闻》

《观察家报》编辑敦促英国公众承认日本吞并满洲国及内蒙古

伦敦3月11日联合通讯社电报道称，《观察家报》主编加宾先生（Mr. Garbin(?)）于3月10日在该报发表了一篇关于远东事务的文章，文中敦促公众承认对满洲国和内蒙古的吞并：-
“除非解决远东问题，否则世界裁军永远无法实现。令人担忧的是，只要列强政府不能采取处理远东问题的方案，危险将始终存在。包括日本在内的所有列强必须同意一项十年和平计划。为了实现这一提议，列强必须遵守一个条件，即承认日本吞并满洲国及部分内蒙古。在考虑中日关系时，必须从地理和经济角度承认日本的地位。尚不清楚日本是否会坚持在华特权，还是满足于财政担保。解决远东问题是最困难的事情，但采取政治性和建设性的方案将应对这一局面。”

pages.en:
March 10, 1935.
Morning Translation
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY. No. D 3753 Date 10. 3. 35.）

MISCELLANEOUS

MAINICHI

JAPANESE MINISTER ARIYOSHI RETURNS TO SHANGHAI

Mr. Ariyoshi, Japanese
Minister to China, returned from Nanking at 7 a.m.
yesterday. In an interview granted to Japanese
newspaper reporters he made the following statement:-
"It is recognized that the
Nanking Government is endeavouring to suppress all
anti-Japanese activities throughout China after Chiang
Kai-Shek and Wang Ching Wei had issued their declaration
regarding Sino-Japanese co-operation. Further
request has been made to the Nanking Government to
do its utmost to suppress anti-Japanese activities.
As regards a foreign loan to China, Mr. T.V. Soong a
few years ago tried to float a loan in America and in
November, 1934 a loan was sought from the Hongkong-
Shanghai Bank. In both cases China failed to secure
a loan. As regards the relations between Japan and
China, the people of the two countries must first be more
closely associated. I know nothing about any loan to
China. I may meet Sir Cadogan, British Minister to
China, when he comes to Shanghai from Nanking. I
believe China will never accept a loan which will prove
harmful to her. I have not heard anything about a
revision of the customs tariff. In connection with the
removal of the office of the Legation to Nanking,
nothing can be said now because preparations for the
removal will require time and instructions must be
secured from the Foreign Office."

NICHI-NICHI

THE JAPANESE AMALGAMATED ASSOCIATION OF STREET UNIONS
AND THE MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS

At 4 p.m. yesterday the
Standing Committee of the Japanese Amalgamated Association
of Street Unions held a meeting at its office
to discuss the Municipal elections.
It is reported that the
Committee will hold another meeting to discuss the
matter.

1935年3月10日。
晨间译件
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特别分部登记处。编号 D 3753 日期 1935年3月10日。）

杂项

《每日新闻》

日本公使有吉明返回上海

日本驻华公使有吉先生于昨日早晨7点从南京返回。在接受日本报社记者采访时，他发表了以下声明：-
“众所周知，在蒋介石和汪精卫发表关于中日合作的宣言后，南京政府正努力镇压全中国的反日活动。已向南京政府进一步提出要求，请其尽力镇压反日活动。关于对华外国贷款，宋子文先生几年前曾试图在美国发行贷款，并于1934年11月向汇丰银行寻求贷款。在这两种情况下，中国均未能获得贷款。关于中日关系，两国人民必须首先更加紧密地联系。我对任何对华贷款一无所知。当英国驻华公使卡多根爵士（Sir Cadogan）从南京来到上海时，我可能会与他会面。我相信中国绝不会接受对其有害的贷款。我没有听到任何关于修改关税的消息。关于公使馆迁往南京一事，目前无可奉告，因为搬迁准备工作需要时间，且必须获得外交部的指示。”

《日日新闻》

日本街道工会联合会与市政选举

昨日下午4时，日本街道工会联合会常务委员会在其办事处举行会议，讨论市政选举事宜。
据悉，委员会将再次举行会议讨论此事。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 3753
Date 8. 1 3 / 35

March 8, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

NIPPO

FURTHER EFFORT TO DEAL WITH ANTI-JAPANESE ACTIVITIES

A Dentsu telegram from
Nanking reports that at 3 p.m. March 7 Mr. Ariyoshi,
Japanese Minister to China, in company with Mr. Arino,
Secretary of the Japanese Legation, called on Mr. Wang
Ching Wei, President of the Executive Yuan, at his
official residence and conferred with him for about
one hour and 50 minutes. It is a matter for
congratulation that the Nanking Government is making
every effort to suppress anti-Japanese activities
after Chiang Kai Shek and Wang Ching Wei had announced
themselves in favour of Sino-Japanese co-operation
for the sake of peace in the Orient.
Mr. Ariyoshi frankly requested
Mr. Wang Ching Wei to redouble his efforts to suppress
anti-Japanese activities. After clearly explaining
Mr. Hirota's fundamental policy towards China, Mr.
Ariyoshi enquired about the intentions of China
regarding a British-American loan to China.
In reply, Mr. Wang Ching Wei
first expressed his thanks to Mr. Ariyoshi for the
warm welcome extended to Dr. Wang Chung Hui during
the latter's stay in Japan. He declared that China
will not show less sincerity than Japan for Sino-
Japanese co-operation because Dr. Wang Chung Hui has
informed the Nanking Government that he was satisfied
with the sincerity of Japan for Sino-Japanese co-operation.
Mr. Wang Ching Wei further informed Mr. Ariyoshi
that he was determined to do his utmost to bring
about an effective suppression of anti-Japanese
activities. In conclusion, he said that China had
not requested Great Britain or the United States for
a loan and that China has not even the intention to
request a loan.

EDUCATION MINISTRY ORDERS MISSIONARY SCHOOLS
NOT TO USE ANTI-JAPANESE TEXT BOOKS

The Ministry of Education
at Nanking has issued an order to all American
missionary schools not to use text books containing
anti-Japanese lessons.
So far the report could not
be confirmed. It is said that all the Government
and private schools will be given similar orders.

SUPERINTENDENT NAKAGAWA TO RETIRE FROM S.M.P.

Superintendent Nakagawa
is reported to be retiring from the S.M.P. at the
beginning of May in accordance with Municipal regulations
as he has reached the age of 59 years.
He rendered valuable service
to the Council during his 25 years service. He is
one of the indispensable officers of the S.M.P. but he
is retiring in order to encourage junior officers.
It is reported that Chief
Inspector Kasumi will be promoted to Superintendent.

编号 D 3753
日期 1935年3月8日

1935年3月8日。午后译件。

杂项

《日报》

进一步努力处理反日活动

南京电通社电报道称，3月7日下午3时，日本驻华公使有吉先生在 Japanese Legation Secretary Arino（音译：有野）秘书的陪同下，前往行政院院长汪精卫先生的官邸拜访，并与他会谈了约1小时50分钟。在蒋介石和汪精卫宣布为了东方和平而支持中日合作后，南京政府正竭尽全力镇压反日活动，这是一件值得祝贺的事。
有吉先生坦率地请求汪精卫先生加倍努力镇压反日活动。在清楚解释了广田先生对华基本政策后，有吉先生询问了中国关于英美对华贷款的意向。
作为回应，汪精卫先生首先感谢有吉先生在王宠惠博士访日期间给予的热情接待。他宣称，既然王宠惠博士已告知南京政府，他对日本在中日合作方面的诚意感到满意，那么中国在这一点上表现出的诚意不会少于日本。汪精卫先生进一步告知有吉先生，他决心尽最大努力有效镇压反日活动。最后，他表示中国并未向英国或美国请求贷款，甚至没有请求贷款的意图。

教育部命令教会学校不得使用反日教科书

南京教育部已向所有美国教会学校发布命令，禁止使用包含反日课程的教科书。
截至目前，该报告尚未得到证实。据悉，所有公立和私立学校都将收到类似的命令。

中川警司将从上海公共租界工部局警务处退休

据悉，中川警司因年满59岁，将根据市政规定于5月初从上海公共租界工部局警务处退休。
他在25年的服役期间为工部局提供了宝贵的服务。他是上海公共租界工部局警务处不可或缺的官员之一，但他为了鼓励初级警官而选择退休。
据悉，霞美（Kasumi，音译）总巡长将晋升为警司。

S. B. RICHTER
No. D 3753
Date 23. 2. 35.

February 23, 1935. Morning Translation

NICHI NICHI

JAPANESE CONSTABLE OF S.M.P. ATTEMPTS SUICIDE

At 9.10 p.m. yesterday
Japanese Constable Matsuta, age 27, attached to Wayside
Police Station called on Japanese Constable Sakai of
Dixwell Road Station at No. 55 Lane 249 North Szechuen
Road and told him that he had come to bid him farewell.
On noticing that Matsuta did not appear normal Sakai
warned him that he was on duty whereupon Matsuta produced
his service pistol and shot himself in the neck. He
was immediately removed to the Fcc King Hospital. His
condition is reported to be very serious.
A letter written before he
attempted suicide reads as follows:-
"My past life was most unhappy.
There will be no happiness in all my life. My life
might have been my father's life. I ask your assistance
after my death."

ANTI-JAPANESE BOYCOTT MOVEMENT IN SOOCHOW

A Soochow telegram dated
February 22 reports that the anti-Japanese boycott there
is being continued with the assistance of the district
Kuomintang. All merchants have been forbidden to
purchase Japanese goods.
The district Kuomintang
called a meeting of officers of various business
organizations at the Chamber of Commerce on February 12
and passed the following resolutions:-
1. All merchants should deal in native products
only and dealing in foreign products which are indispensible
must be stopped gradually.
2. The sales books of all firms must be subject
to the inspection of the Kuomintang.
3. The business circles must be in close
connection with the Kuomintang in order to enforce the
boycott of foreign products and to encourage the use of
native goods.

MAINICHI

JAPANESE ARRESTED IN CONNECTION WITH PASSING OF
COUNTERFEIT BANK NOTES

The Japanese Consular Police
arrested 4 Japanese named Matsushima, Chiyoki Orita(female),
Mori and Mudo on suspicion of passing counterfeit bank
notes. They have meantime been sentenced to imprisonment
for contravening the Japanese Consulate regulations.

1935年2月23日。晨间译件

《日日新闻》

上海公共租界工部局警务处日本巡捕企图自杀

昨晚9时10分，隶属于路边巡捕房（Wayside Police Station）的27岁日本巡捕松田（Matsuta）前往北四川路249弄55号狄思威路巡捕房的日本巡捕酒井（Sakai）处，告诉他自己前来道别。酒井注意到松田神色异常，警告他正在执勤，随即松田掏出配枪朝自己颈部开枪。他立即被送往福金医院（Fcc King Hospital）。据悉他的情况非常危急。
他在企图自杀前写的一封信内容如下：-
“我的过去生活极其不幸。我的一生都不会有幸福。我的生命本应是我父亲的生命。我死后请求你们的帮助。”

苏州的反日抵制运动

2月22日苏州电报道称，当地的反日抵制运动在区国民党的协助下仍在继续。所有商人均被禁止购买日本货物。
区国民党于2月12日在商会召集各商业组织负责人开会，并通过以下决议：-
1. 所有商人应只经营国货，对于必需的外国商品，必须逐步停止交易。
2. 所有商号的销货簿必须接受国民党的检查。
3. 商界必须与国民党保持密切联系，以执行对外国商品的抵制并鼓励使用国货。

《每日新闻》

日本人因使用假钞被捕

日本领事警察逮捕了4名日本人，分别是松岛（Matsushima）、折田千代喜（Chiyoki Orita，女）、森（Mori）和武藤（Mudo），嫌疑是使用假钞。与此同时，他们因违反日本领事馆规定被判监禁。

February 23, 1935. Morning Translation.

MAINICHI
D6501
GENERAL DOIHARA RETURNS TO SHANGHAI
Major-General Doihara
returned to Shanghai at 7 a.m. yesterday from Nanking.
On February 25 the General will issue a statement re-
garding the result of the conferences held with the
Chinese officials recently. He will leave Shanghai
for Hongkong and Canton on February 26 on the S.S.
"Terukuni Maru". Major Ichita will accompany the
General on the trip.
X

NIPPO
D3753
CHANG HSUEH LIANG EXPENDS $100,000 FOR ANTI-
JAPANESE MOVEMENT
KONG TEK PAH TAKES ACTIVE PART

A Chinese named Kong Tek Fah,
ex-officer of the Foreign Affairs Bureau in Honan
Province, and a notorious anti-Japanese writer, is
reported to have been given $100,000 by Chang Hsueh
Liang for the purpose of creating obstruction to the
promotion of Sino-Japanese relations which has recently
been proposed. Kong Tek Fah is the author of the
"Secret Diplomatic History of Japan's Invasion in China",
"Disclosure of Japan's Plot" and "The Truth of the
Nishihara Loan".

He received the sum of money
with a definite understanding of making agitation
against Japanese. This proves that Chang Hsueh Liang
is still holding anti-Japanese ideas.

1935年2月23日。晨间译件。

《每日新闻》
D6501
土肥原将军返回上海
土肥原少将于昨日早晨7点从南京返回上海。该将军将于2月25日发表声明，说明近期与中国官员举行会议的结果。他将于2月26日乘坐“照国丸”轮离开上海前往香港和广州。市田大尉（Major Ichita，音译）将陪同将军同行。
X

《日报》
D3753
张学良花费10万美元用于反日运动
孔德法积极参与

据悉，一名名叫孔德法（Kong Tek Fah）的中国人，前任河南省外事局官员，也是一名臭名昭著的反日作家，从张学良那里获得了10万美元，目的是阻碍最近提出的促进中日关系的发展。孔德法是《日本侵华秘密外交史》、《揭露日本阴谋》和《西原借款真相》的作者。

他收下这笔钱时明确理解是要进行反日煽动。这证明张学良仍然持有反日思想。

February 18, 1935.

Political (4)

Anti-Japanese Movement - shops attacked in
Western District

D.3753

At 7.40 p.m. February 16, glass panes of the show
windows of the following concerns were either shattered
or pierced by small iron balls, believed to have been
shot from a bow :-

Ta Sing Photo Studio, 960 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.
Ta Loh Sock Shop, 3 Brenan Road, O.O.L.
Tien Loh Confectionery Shop, 7 Brenan Road, O.O.L.
Kuo Hwa Shop, 11 Brenan Road, O.O.L.
Tien Tsin Shoe Shop, 56 Brenan Road, O.O.L.
Yao Hwa Photo Studio, 554 Connaught Road, O.O.L.

In the case of Ta Sing Photo Studio and the Ta Loh
Sock Shop, copies of a notice to the following effect were
found inside the doors of the shops :

"Yesterday we used iron balls but tomorrow we will
use bullets. He who repents first will obtain the
light of salvation before the others".

Simultaneously the Tien Loh Confectionery Shop
received a notice on which was written "What we did
yesterday was just a warning to you to correct your wrongs."

All these slips purport to emanate from the
"Breast Beating Group lamenting the Nation" (椎胸痛國團).
The Ta Loh Sock Shop has consequently posted a notice on
its door, announcing that it ceased dealing in Japanese
goods a long time ago.

D.3753

2月16日晚7时40分，下列商号的橱窗玻璃或被砸碎，或被疑似从弓弩射出的小铁球击穿：

大生照相馆，极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）960号，越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
大罗袜店，白利南路（Brenan Road）3号，越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
天罗糖果店，白利南路（Brenan Road）7号，越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
国华商店，白利南路（Brenan Road）11号，越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
天津鞋店，白利南路（Brenan Road）56号，越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
耀华照相馆，康纳脱路（Connaught Road）554号，越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。

在大生照相馆和大罗袜店两案中，在店门内发现了内容如下的通告副本：

“昨日吾等使用铁球，明日将使用子弹。率先悔悟者，将先于他人获得救赎之光”。

与此同时，天罗糖果店收到一份通告，上面写着：“昨日之所为，仅是警告尔等改正错误。”

所有这些纸条均声称出自“椎胸痛国团”。因此，大罗袜店已在门上张贴告示，宣布其早已停止经营日货。

NANKING HUOMINTANG BOYCOTT JAPANESE GOODS

A Nanking telegram dated
February 19 reports that a few days ago the District
Kuomintang issued instructions to the hotels and restaurants
in Nanking prohibiting the use of Japanese sea products.

Upon learning of the matter,
the Japanese Consular authorities at Nanking called at
the Foreign Ministry and lodged a verbal protest against
the action and requested the Ministry to deal with the
matter.

Subject (in full) Chinese Chamber of Commerce receives secret instruction
from local Kuomintang.
Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by Whouman ASS.

On May 13, the Chinese Chamber of Commerce
issued a secret circular instruction to local trade
associations quoting a confidential order from the
local Kuomintang. The order states that the
Japanese authorities have repeatedly lodged protests
with the Tangpu against the denunciation of Japanese
products in the Chinese press. The Tangpu
instructs the Chamber of Commerce to refrain from
using the word "Japanese" when mentioning products
of that country in any documents in future. Other
words like LIEH (劣) (bad) can be used in place
of the character "Japanese", the instruction concludes.

C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 3753
January Due 30/1/34

Political (2)

Chamber of Commerce - inspects sealed iron of Japanese
origin

At 2 p.m. January 23, Li Da-chwang (李如祥), a
staff employee of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, in
company with Koo Hung-chao (顾鸿诏) and Zung Sa-ming
(郑世铭), committee members of the Iron Trade
Association (10 Hongkong Road) visited in the name of
the Chamber and the Association in question, the Ziang Tai
(祥泰) Iron Hong, 324/5/6 North Soochow Road, and
inspected the 5,896 sealed Japanese iron bars in its
possession, in order to ascertain that none of them had
been disposed of. The inspection lasted about
an hour.

It will be recalled that on October 4, 1933, the
Iron Trade Association discovered the presence of about
100 tons of iron bars of Japanese origin on the premises
of the Ziang Feng Foundry (祥丰), 1174 East
Yuhang Road. This Foundry, claiming that the iron
belonged to the Ziang Tai Iron Hong, removed same to the
Hong on North Soochow Road, where the iron was sealed
by the Association on the same day.

Aviation Construction Movement - fund contributed by the
Nanyang Brothers Tobacco Factory

At 2 p.m. January 29, the Nanyang Brothers Tobacco
Factory sent a cheque for $5,000 to the office of the
China Aviation Cooperative Society, Chinese Y.M.C.A.
building, 438 Boulevard de Montigny, as a contribution
towards the aviation construction fund.

政治类 (2)

商会 - 检查封存的日源铁条

1月23日下午2时，中国商会职员李如祥（Li Da-chwang），会同铁业公会（香港路10号）委员顾鸿诏（Koo Hung-chao）和郑世铭（Zung Sa-ming），以商会及相关公会的名义，走访了位于北苏州路324/5/6号的祥泰（Ziang Tai）铁行，检查了其拥有的5,896根封存的日本铁条，以确认其中没有任何一根被处置。检查持续了约一小时。

需回顾的是，1933年10月4日，铁业公会在东余杭路1174号的祥丰（Ziang Feng）铸造厂 premises 发现了约100吨日源铁条。该铸造厂声称这些铁条属于祥泰铁行，遂将其移至北苏州路的铁行，铁条于当日由公会封存。

航空建设运动 - 南洋兄弟烟草厂捐款

1月29日下午2时，南洋兄弟烟草厂向蒙太尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）438号中华基督教青年会大楼内的中国航空协进会办公室发送了一张5,000美元的支票，作为对航空建设基金的捐款。

September 12, 1933.    2.    Morning Translation
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY No. D 375-3 Date 1/1 9.1 33）

LABOUR.

Interviewed yesterday by a reporter of the Sing Sung News Agency, Sun Hua-zung, Chairman of the Silk Filature Owners Association, stated that the strike was instigated by undesirables and that the Association had decided to request the Social Bureau and the local Tangpu to promulgate the date for the re-opening of all filatures and to instruct the Public Safety Bureau to arrest the agitators.

MISCELLANEOUS

China Times and other local newspapers:

THE BOYCOTT OF JAPANESE GOODS.

The Copper and Iron Machine Trade Association is keeping a close watch for enemy iron.
Of late, the Association has discovered that the Hong Shing Chong (項興昌) Factory had purchased about ten tons of enemy iron. As a result of repeated strong negotiations, the Hong Shing Chong factory has returned the enemy iron to the Sen Shin Company (千信洋行) and expressed its willingness to pay $600, the value of the enemy iron, to the Association as a fine. This was rejected by the Association and towards the end of August the factory published an apology to the Association swearing to buy native iron in future.
The Association has also opened strong negotiations with the Ziang Foong (祥豐) Factory for using sealed enemy iron. The factory has also secretly purchased 360 tons of Indian Iron.
It is learned that the Association has written to the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce asking for instructions.

THE ASSOCIATION OF CHINESE CHARTERED ACCOUNTANTS.

It is learned that the Association of Chinese Chartered Accountants, which was inaugurated the day before yesterday in the Chinese Y.M.C.A., Boulevard de Montigny, will hold section examination meetings at 10 a.m. to-day.
At 2 p.m. the delegates of the Association will pay a visit to the Clearing House, No.4 Hongkong Road, and at 4 p.m. they will attend a reception tendered them by the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce.

September 7, 1933.    Morning Translation

MISCELLANEOUS

NIPPO

JAPANESE COMMITS SUICIDE

At 12.20 p.m. yesterday the Japanese Consular Police received information that a Japanese named H. Bokuki(?), 27, an employee of the Marusan Dispensary No. 62 Burkall Road, had committed suicide. and Detective Sato and Dr. Tongu of the Foo Ming Hospital were dispatched to the scene. The doctor found that the deceased had killed himself with a sharp spear. The dead man left 4 letters addressed to his father, mother, his employer and brother.

CHINESE CHAMBER AND THE BOYCOTT OF JAPANESE GOODS

The Chinese Chamber of Commerce, the chairman of which is Mr. Wang Hsao Lian, is supporting the Anti-Japanese boycott. Recently it decided to hold an exhibition of Japanese goods in order to bring about a stronger boycott.

The Chamber has issued invitations to all Chinese business organizations to exhibit samples of Japanese goods which they are dealing in order to enable the public to distinguish Japanese goods from other goods.

FOREIGN EMPLOYEE OF N.Y.K. ASSAULTED IN CHAPEL

At 5 p.m. September Mr. C.S. O'Brien, an employee of the N.Y.K. Passenger Department and his wife, both British subjects, were surrounded by a crowd of Chinese loafers in Chapel when the foreigners drove his private motor car into Chapel without a Chinese license. One of the loafers dragged Mrs. O'Brien out of the motor car and accused her with driving the motor car into Chapel without a Chinese license. When Mr. O'Brien attempted to effect the release of his wife from the loafers, the latter attacked Mrs. O'Brien tearing her dress. Mr. O'Brien managed to get away from the scene and proceeded to Hongkew Police Station where he reported the incident and added that a Chinese policeman who arrived on the scene attempted to draw his pistol instead of dispersing the loafers.

AMERICAN SAILOR ASSAULTS JAPANESE SHOP ASSISTANT.

日本人自杀

昨日中午12时20分，日本领事警察接到情报称，一名名叫 H. Bokuki(?)（音译）、27岁的日本人，系伯基尔路（Burkall Road）62号丸山药房（Marusan Dispensary）职员，已自杀身亡。佐藤（Sato）侦探和福明医院（Foo Ming Hospital）的 Tongu 医生被派往现场。医生发现死者是用尖矛自杀的。死者留下了4封信，分别写给其父亲、母亲、雇主和兄弟。

中国商会与抵制日货

由中国商会主席王筱莲（Wang Hsao Lian，音译）领导的中国商会支持反日抵制运动。最近，商会决定举办日货展览，以推动更强烈的抵制行动。

商会已向所有华商组织发出邀请，要求展出其经营的日货样品，以便公众区分日货与其他商品。

纽约轮船公司外籍雇员在乍浦路遭袭

9月某日下午5时，纽约轮船公司客运部雇员、英籍人士 C.S. O'Brien 先生及其妻子在乍浦路（Chapel）驾车驶入该路时，因未持有中国执照，被一群中国闲散人员包围。其中一名闲散人员将 O'Brien 夫人拖出汽车，指责她无中国执照驾车进入乍浦路。当 O'Brien 先生试图从闲散人员手中解救其妻子时，后者袭击了 O'Brien 夫人，撕破了她的衣服。O'Brien 先生设法逃离现场，前往虹口警察局报案，并补充说，一名到达现场的中国警察非但没有驱散闲散人员，反而试图拔出手枪。

该团体约有六十名成员，大多为年轻学生或工人，他们曾在中日敌对行动期间作为志愿者，与第十九路军并肩参加上海保卫战。

该团体实施袭击所使用的手榴弹，均为中国国民革命军采用的制式型号。这些手榴弹要么来自第十九路军，要么来自高昌庙兵工厂，该厂的所有弹药库存刚刚通过铁路运往南京。

据称，这个“爱国”协会得到以下人士的支持：商会主席王晓籁（WANG SHAO LAN）、律师吴迈（OU MAI）、北京政府前内务总长熊希龄（HSIUNG SHI LING）、商会会员郑澄传（ZHENG TSING TSING）、租界公民联合会会员胡凤翔（HU FENG HSIANG）、律师沈钧儒（SUH TSOU ZE）以及低级邮务员工会会员、前救国委员会成员陆京士（LOH KING ZE）。该团体在旅馆、各协会或工会内举行秘密会议。已组织募捐以资助该团体。

民众救国会（设于古林路景安里29号）通过派人到各家商店调查，以确定哪些商人仍在销售日货，从而协助该团体。由此获得的情报被

Les autres groupes similaires: groupe qui agit par le fer

Il est à noter que la campagne d'intimidation des marchands

elle incite jusqu'à un certain point les commerçants à renouveler
avec des marchandises chinoises similaires, les stocks de produits

其他类似团体包括：“铁血锄奸团”、“红血锄奸团”、“孤儿锄奸团”等，据称是由一些不择手段的人组织的，他们企图从某些轻信他们的天真人士那里骗取钱财。

值得注意的是，恐吓“奸商”的运动对某些上海商人有利，因为在一定程度上，这促使商人们用类似的国货来补充他们正在抛售或藏匿的日货库存。/

This group comprises sixty members who are, for the
most part, young students or workers who have participated
as volunteers in the defence of Shanghai, side by side with
the 19th army during the Sino-Japanese hostilities.
The grenades used by this group in the perpetration
of their attempts are all of the model adopted by the
National Chinese Army. They come from either the 19th
Route Army or the Kaotchangmiao Arsenal whose entire
stock of munitions has been transferred by rail to Nanking.
This "patriotic" association is being supported, it
is said, by Wang SHAO LAN, President of the Chamber of
Commerce ( 王晓籁 ), OU KAI ( 吴邁 ), lawyer,
HSIUNG SHI LING ( 熊希龄 ) Former Minister for the

Member of the Chamber of Commerce, HU FENG HSIANG ( 胡鳳翔 )
Member of the Union of Citizens of the Settlement, SUN TSOU ZE

are held in the hotels or associations or syndicates.
Subscriptions have been collected to assist the association.
The People's Association for the National Salvation
(installed at No. 29 Kitb Zeng An Li, Kuling Road) is

in the different stores with a view to ascertaining who

Information thus obtained is communicated to the group
whose members offer themselves body and soul for the
extermination of the treacherous merchants. These latter
send letters of warning or throw bombs into the shops of
the proprietors who are considered guilty.

该团体由六十名成员组成，其中大多数是年轻学生或工人，他们在中日敌对行动期间作为志愿者，与第十九路军并肩参加上海保卫战。
该团体在实施袭击时使用的手榴弹，均为中国国民革命军采用的制式型号。这些手榴弹要么来自第十九路军，要么来自高昌庙兵工厂，该厂的所有弹药库存已通过铁路转移至南京。
据称，这个“爱国”协会得到以下人士的支持：商会主席王晓籁（Wang SHAO LAN）、律师吴迈（OU KAI）、北京政府前内务总长熊希龄（HSIUNG SHI LING）、商会会员郑清（TSENG TSENG TSING）、租界公民联合会会员胡凤翔（HU FENG HSIANG）、律师沈钧儒（SUN TSOU ZE）以及低级邮务员工会会员、前救国委员会成员陆京士（LOH KING ZE）。其秘密会议在旅馆、协会或工会内举行。已募集捐款以资助该协会。
民众救国会（设于古林路景安里29号）通过派人到各家商店进行调查，以确定哪些商人仍在继续销售日货，从而协助该团体。由此获得的情报被传达给该团体，其成员誓死致力于铲除奸商。后者向被认为有罪的店主发出警告信，或向其店铺投掷炸弹。

pages.en:
- 3 -

Other similar groups are as follows:- The group
of Blood and Iron for the extermination of treacherous
merchants, the group of Red Blood for the extermination
of treacherous merchants, Group of madcaps for the
extermination of treacherous merchants, etc. and these
are organised by several unscrupulous persons whose sole
purpose is to extort money from certain naive persons,
who are prepared to believe them.
    Note should be taken of the fact that the campaign
of intimidation of the "treacherous" merchants is advantageous
to some Shanghai dealers as it prompts, to a certain extent,
                    their stores in lieu of
the merchants to replenish/the Japanese stock of products,
which they either dispose of or hide by similar Chinese
merchandise.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

其他类似团体如下：- “铁血锄奸团”、“红血锄奸团”、“狂人锄奸团”等，这些团体由几个不择手段的人组织，其唯一目的是从某些准备相信他们的天真人士那里勒索钱财。
    应注意这一事实：恐吓“奸商”的运动对某些上海商人有利，因为它在一定程度上促使
                    他们的商店用类似的国货
来补充/替换他们正在处理或藏匿的日货产品库存。

C. & S. B. REGISTRY
N. D. 3753/
Date 5 / 4 / 32

Translation of a poster posted on the wall at
the corner of Avenue Edward VII and Thibet Road
--------

The Evening News of the 24th carried a report to
the effect that some Chinese emigrants in Japan happened
to discover from an English letter picked up in a
restaurant in Yokohama that the "Japanese Military
Medical School" are studying ways to infect the merchandize
to be transported to China with poisonous medicine with
the object of eliminating our nation. In order that
the public will not be deceived the letter is copied
down hereunder:-

"I have to inform you that in October 1931, the Japanese
Imperial Military Medical School has organized a
'Medicine for Poisoning Chinese People Research Society'
with a view to infect daily necessities with poisonous
medicine by scientific methods. People will be rendered
unable to bear children should they become infected
with a species of medicine contained in clothing while
others will suffer from Cholera should they use certain
kinds of toilet articles infected with poison. As we
reside in China we should therefore be more careful.
Besides requesting our Government to notify the people
I hereby inform you as well".

Notices    Nationals

张贴在爱多亚路与西藏路转角墙上的海报译文
--------

24日的《字林西报》刊登了一则报道，大意是有些在日本的中国侨民偶然从横滨一家餐馆捡到的一封英文信中得知，“日本陆军军医学校”正在研究用毒药感染将运往中国的商品的方法，目的是消灭我国民族。为了使公众不受欺骗，现将该信抄录如下：-

“我必须通知你们，1931年10月，日本帝国陆军军医学校组织了一个‘毒害中国人药物研究会’，旨在通过科学方法用毒药感染日常生活用品。如果人们感染了衣物中含有的某种药物，将无法生育；而如果使用了某些被毒药感染的卫生用品，则会患上霍乱。由于我们居住在中国，因此应更加小心。除了请求我国政府通知民众外，我特此告知你们”。

通告    同胞们

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. REGISTRY
D 2753/1
Date November 3, 1932.

Subject (in full) Anti-Japanese Movement

Made by and Forwarded by Superintendent Robertson.

With reference to attached translation of
extract from the "Nippo" of November 2, both the
Municipal and French Police are doing all they can to
suppress any movement which aims at menacing the peace
of the local community. It is true that anti-
Japanese bodies have come into existence since the
cessation of the Shanghai hostilities and coinciding
with Japan's campaign in Manchuria but so long as these
confine themselves to activities which do not contravene
the Criminal Code of the Republic of China or the
Municipal Bye-laws the Municipal Police are powerless
to interfere. What the Japanese would like is
arbitrary measures, but such would possibly do more
harm than good and would be certain to react on the
S.M.C.

The matter of intimidation of shops by the
throwing of grenades and threats is receiving the
attention of both police forces, but it must be conceded
that their efforts in this direction have been greatly
hampered by lack of cooperation on the part of the
victims themselves coupled with the fact that the
average member of the Chinese community is only too
willing at the moment to overlook any offence, no matter how
heinous, so long as it is in the interest of the anti-
Japanese movement.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (CRIME BRANCH)）
（批：109）
（批：Supt）
（批：5p）

Thos Robertson
Superintendent.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
（批：(Crime) Information and form of passing to Commissioner of Police. W. Edwards 4/11/32）

特别处，第一科
报告
档案号 登记室
D 2753/1
日期 1932年11月3日。

主题（全称）反日运动

由罗伯逊警司制作并转发。

关于附带的11月2日《日日新闻》摘录译文，公共租界警务处和法租界警务处都在尽其所能镇压任何旨在威胁本地社区和平的运动。诚然，自上海战事停止并与日本在满洲的行动 coinciding 以来，反日团体已经出现，但只要这些团体的活动不违反《中华民国刑法》或《工部局附律》，公共租界警务处便无权干涉。日本人希望的是任意采取强制措施，但这可能弊大于利，并肯定会对工部局产生反作用。

通过投掷手榴弹和威胁来恐吓商店的问题正受到两个警务处的关注，但必须承认，由于受害者本身缺乏合作，加上目前华人社区的一般成员只要符合反日运动的利益，就过于愿意忽略任何罪行，无论其多么恶劣，这两个警务处在此方面的努力受到了极大阻碍。

（印章：副总监（刑事处））
（批注：109）
（批注：警司）
（批注：5页）

Thos Robertson

The North Eastern Volunteer Army Support Committee
came into existence on April 18, 1932 (Vide I.R. 10/4/32)
and the principal promotors include Chu Wei-sen, Chairman
of the Chekiang Provincial Association, Feng Sao-san,
(馮少山), Member of the Kwang Zau Guild and Li Tsz-san,
member of the Shanghai Bar Association. So far as can
be ascertained, the only activities of this body up to
the present are confined to endeavours to raise funds by
soliciting contributions to support the North Eastern
Volunteer Armies.

'All Chinese Amalgamated Association of the
National Salvation Association otherwise known as
Federation of National Salvation Bodies of Various
Circles in China came into existence during meetings
held between October 30 and November 1 (Vide I.R.2/11/32).
No practical activities have yet come to notice although
resolutions of the usual so-called "patriotic" nature
were passed. The principal promoter is one named
Chang Chun-kwang who seems to belong to the "Western
Hills" clique.
pages.zh:
东北义勇军后援会于1932年4月18日成立（参见1932年4月10日情报报告），主要发起人包括浙江省同乡会主席朱蔚生、广东会馆会员冯少山（Feng Sao-san）以及上海律师公会会员李子三。据查，该团体迄今为止的唯一活动仅限于通过 soliciting 捐款来筹集资金，以支持东北义勇军。

“全中国各界救国联合会”，又称“中国各界救国团体联合会”，于10月30日至11月1日期间举行的会议上成立（参见1932年11月2日情报报告）。虽然通过了通常所谓的“爱国”性质的决议，但尚未发现任何实际行动。主要发起人名叫张春广，他似乎属于“西山会议派”。

Shanghai November 2, 1932.

Translation of Report on Enquiry No.II3/s.
------------------------------------------

According to an enquiry the group which is offering
itself body and soul to exterminate the "treacherous"
merchants has been secretly organised by the following
persons who were members of the Committee for National
Salvation and whose activity extended to the attack on
Shanghai by the Japanese:-
ZENG ZANG SENG (曾長森) former student of the Fudan
University and former second commander of
the group which had to proceed to North-East
with a view to assisting General MA CHEN SHAN.
FAN ZENG LIANG (范仁良 ) Chief of the Section in
communication with the Corps of hospital
attendants on volunteers of North-East.
ZHENG YA FOU (陳亞夫 ) former Chief Commander of the
Shanghai Volunteers.
YING TSE LING (殷芝齡) Member of the Federation of
89 organisations for the National Salvation.
ZENG PEI TEH (陳培德 ) Member of the General Workers'
Syndicate.
TSAI YAI HSI (蔡耀意 ) Former Secretary of the
Military Headquarters of Shanghai Volunteers.
TAI PAH TSE (談伯質 ) Member of the People's
Association for National Salvation.
TSANG KUIN KWANG (張年光 ) Commander of the 19th
company
Advance army/disbanded recently .

1932年11月11日

上海法租界。
政治警务处。

上海，1932年11月2日。

第II3/s号调查报告译文。
------------------------------------------

经调查，这个誓死致力于铲除“奸商”的团体由以下人员秘密组织，这些人曾是救国委员会成员，其活动范围延伸至日军进攻上海期间：-
曾长森（ZENG ZANG SENG），复旦大学前学生，曾任赴东北协助马占山将军部队的副指挥官。
范仁良（FAN ZENG LIANG），负责与东北志愿军医护队联络的科室主任。
陈亚夫（ZHENG YA FOU），上海义勇军前总指挥。
殷芝龄（YING TSE LING），八十九个救国团体联合会成员。
陈培德（ZENG PEI TEH），总工会成员。
蔡耀意（TSAI YAI HSI），上海义勇军军事总部前秘书。
谈伯质（TAI PAH TSE），民众救国会成员。
张年光（TSANG KUIN KWANG），第十九连连长。
先遣部队/最近已解散。

pages.en:
- 2 -

This group comprises sixty members who are, for the
most part, young students or workers who have participated
as volunteers in the defence of Shanghai, side by side with
the 19th army during the Sino-Japanese hostilities.
The grenades used by this group in the perpetration
of their attempts are all of the model adopted by the
National Chinese Army. They come from either the 19th
Route Army or the Kaotchangmiao Arsenal whose entire
stock of munitions has been transferred by rail to Nanking.
This "patriotic" association is being supported, it
is said, by Wang SHAO LAN, President of the Chamber of
Commerce (王晓籁), OU HAI (吴邁), lawyer,
HSIUNG SHI LING (熊希齡) Former Minister for the
Interior of the Peking Government, TENG TSING TSING (鄭清澄),
Member of the Chamber of Commerce, HU FENG HSIANG (胡鳳翔)
Member of the Union of Citizens of the Settlement, SUN TSCU ZE
(沈鈞儒) lawyer and LOH KING ZE (陸京士), member
of the Junior Postal Employees Syndicate and former Member
of the National Salvation Committee. Its secret meetings
are held in the hotels or associations or syndicates.
Subscriptions have been collected to assist the association.
D: 3701.1 The People's Association for the National Salvation
(installed at No. 29 Kite Zeng An Li, Kuling Road) is
assisting the group by sending out persons to make enquiries
in the different stores with a view to ascertaining who
are the merchants who still continue to sell Japanese goods.
Information thus obtained is communicated to the group
whose members offer themselves body and soul for the
extermination of the treacherous merchants. These latter
send letters of warning or throw bombs into the shops of
the proprietors who are considered guilty.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

该团体由六十名成员组成，他们大多是年轻学生或工人，在中日敌对行动期间，曾作为志愿者与第十九路军并肩参加上海保卫战。
该团体在实施企图时所使用的炸弹，均为中国国民军队所采用的型号。这些炸弹来自第十九路军或高昌庙兵工厂，该兵工厂的全部弹药库存已通过铁路转运至南京。
据称，这个“爱国”协会正得到商会会长王晓籁（Wang SHAO LAN）、律师吴迈（OU HAI）、前北京政府内务总长熊希龄（HSIUNG SHI LING）、商会会员郑清澄（TENG TSING TSING）、租界市民联合会会员胡凤翔（HU FENG HSIANG）、律师沈钧儒（SUN TSCU ZE）以及青年邮务职工会会员、前救国会委员陆京士（LOH KING ZE）的支持。其秘密会议在旅馆、会馆或工会中举行。
已募集捐款以资助该协会。
D: 3701.1 人民救国协会（设于古岭路吉增安里29号）正在协助该团体，派人到各家商店查询，以确定哪些商人仍在继续销售日货。由此获得的情报会通报给该团体，其成员誓死致力于铲除奸商。后者向被视为有罪的店主发出警告信，或向其店铺投掷炸弹。

November 2, 1932.    Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

NIPPO

ANTI JAPANESE ACTIVITIES OF CHINESE COAL MERCHANTS.

The anti-Japanese activities
are becoming more serious in Shanghai as the date of the
general meeting of the League of Nations approaches.
New organizations such as the
"All China Amalgamated Association of the National
Salvation Associations" and the "Support Association of
the Northern-East Volunteer Army" have been formed.
These bodies have been formed by Chinese elements who
are opposed to General Chiang Kai Sek. The Chinese
communists are inciting an anti-Japanese movement amongst
Chinese people while the Blood and Soul Corps is carrying
on its anti-Japanese activities.
Owing to the activities of these
bodies the anti-Japanese movement is likely to become
worse. The Chinese authorities are suppressing anti-
Japanese activities in accordance with the policy already
adopted by the city government. The movement is
being carried out in both the International Settlement
and the French Concession but these foreign authorities
are lukewarm so that the anti-Japanese activities are
becoming graver.
The Chinese Coal Merchants Guild
recently formed a branch association known as "National
Products Branch Association to support the anti-Japanese
boycott movement". On October 31 the guild formed
an Inspection Branch and an Investigation Branch to deal
with Japanese coal.
It is reported that the Inspection
groups will deal severely with any coal merchant who
handles Japanese coal.
The National Government is too
busy to pay attention to the boycott movement. It
will probably impose an anti-dumping tax on Fushun coal.

MAINICHI

FRENCH SOLDIERS ASSAULT KOREAN WOMAN

At 10.00 p.m. November 1, three
French soldiers desiring to find a brothel went to the
first floor of a certain house near the Hanbury Road
Bridge and knocked at the door of a room occupied by
Koreans. As there was no response to the knocking,
the French soldiers broke down the door and entered the
room. The Koreans who were in the room attempted to
run away but were assaulted. The soldiers then entered
the next room and assaulted a Korean woman to such an extent
that she is now unable to walk. At this moment a Chinese
constable of Hongkew Police Station arrived on the scene
and took the soldiers to the station. Later a Japanese
constable named Shimizu removed the Korean woman to the
Foo Ling Hospital.

1932年11月2日。上午译件。

杂项

日日新闻

中国煤商的抗日活动。

随着国际联盟大会日期的临近，上海的抗日活动日趋严重。
“全国救国团体联合总会”和“支援东北义勇军后援会”等新组织已经成立。
这些团体由反对蒋介石将军的中国分子组成。中国共产党人正在中国人民中煽动抗日运动，而铁血团也在进行其抗日活动。
由于这些团体的活动，抗日运动可能会进一步恶化。中国当局正按照市政府已采取的政策镇压抗日活动。该运动在公共租界和法租界均有开展，但这些外国当局态度冷淡，致使抗日活动日益严重。
中国煤业公会最近成立了一个分会，名为“国货支会”，以支持抗日抵制运动。10月31日，该公会成立了检查部和调查部，以处理日煤问题。
据报道，检查组将严厉处置任何经营日煤的煤商。
国民政府忙于他务，无暇顾及抵制运动。它可能会对抚顺煤征收反倾销税。

每日新闻

法国士兵袭击朝鲜妇女

11月1日晚上10时，三名法国士兵为了寻找妓院，前往汉伯里路（Hanbury Road）桥附近某幢房屋的二楼，敲了一间由朝鲜人居住的房间的门。由于敲门无人应答，法国士兵破门而入。屋内的朝鲜人试图逃跑，但遭到殴打。随后，士兵们进入隔壁房间，对一名朝鲜妇女施暴，致其无法行走。此时，虹口巡捕房的一名中国巡警赶到现场，将士兵带往巡捕房。后来，一名名叫清水（Shimizu）的日本巡警将该朝鲜妇女送往福林医院（Foo Ling Hospital）。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, AUGUST 27, 1932

NO IMPROVEMENT IN
LOCAL BOYCOTT
Japanese Look To S.M.C.
To Curb Activities
Of Pickets

The anti-Japanese boycott move-
ment is rapidly becoming worse,
in the opinion of local Japanese
officials. Scarcely a day passes
without numerous instances being
reported of Japanese goods being
confiscated by members of the
boycott organisations or of Japan-
ese merchants being in some way
or other attacked by persons pre-
sumed to be acting under the direc-
tion of such organizations.

In the opinion of these same
officials the situation within the
International Settlement is worse
than that without and the Japan-
ese authorities are looking to the
Settlement authorities, namely, the
Shanghai Municipal Council, to
suppress the movement within its
boundaries.

While not yet as bad, in many
respects, as before the outbreak
of hostilities in January last, the
boycott situation is viewed with
considerable apprehension by
Japanese officials who fear that un-
less steps are taken immediately
to suppress these activities, the
situation may get beyond the
suppressive capabilities of the
S.M.C. and bring about further
Sino-Japanese friction.

（印：FILE O.C./C.S.B）

《字林西报》，1932年8月27日，星期六

本地抵制运动未见改善
日本人指望工部局
遏制纠察队活动

在当地日本官员看来，抗日抵制运动正迅速恶化。几乎每天都有多起事件报告，称抵制组织成员没收日货，或日本商人以某种方式受到 presumed 受此类组织指挥的人员的攻击。

在这些官员看来，公共租界内的局势比界外更糟，日本当局正指望租界当局，即上海公共租界工部局，在其辖区内镇压该运动。

虽然就许多方面而言，抵制局势尚未像去年一月战事爆发前那样糟糕，但日本官员对此深感忧虑，他们担心如果不立即采取措施镇压这些活动，局势可能会超出工部局的镇压能力，并引发进一步的日中摩擦。

（印：FILE O.C./C.S.B）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, August 29, 1932 REGISTRY
No. D 3753
30/8/32

A Stitch In Time
AN EDITORIAL

PROMPT, and it is to be hoped stern, measures are being taken by the City Government of Greater Shanghai to suppress illegal and terroristic activities in connection with the Japanese boycott.
Assurances to that effect have been conveyed to the Japanese Consulate-General as a result of Mayor Wu Te-chen's recent quiet conferences with local business and other leaders.
Even though no miracles instantly result, this development must be construed as a triumph for moderation and sanity on the Chinese side. It should be met with the most thorough-going frankness and coöperation on the part of everyone else; and this coöperation should include recognition of facts which cannot logically be avoided.
One of these facts is that Japan is continuing to afford reason why Chinese, of the most patriotic and law-abiding description, may well desire not to buy Japanese goods. Neither Mayor Wu nor any other Chinese leader can change this situation.
The only power which can change it is Japan herself. All that Chinese leaders can do is to work against violent and illegal acts which not only injure the Japanese, but hurt the boycott cause itself in the eyes of people of every nationality.
Another fact is that control of the Chinese authorities does not extend within the two settlements. This point may seem self-evident, but it should be recognized that the activities of the Chinese "loafer" and racketeer more or less interlock between the settlements and the Chinese areas. Unless the settlements keep their house well in order, the task of the Chinese authorities is made that much harder.
It should also be recognised that Japanese in Shanghai owe a special duty of patience and non-provocation both to the Chinese and to their fellow-foreigners. They are not in their own country; they are in the country of another under peculiarly difficult circumstances. Thus should avoid everything savouring of arrogance, particularly in view of recent happenings both in Shanghai and Manchuria.
Tactful policies on the part of the Japanese military, civil and business leaders can go far toward easing the law enforcement tasks of Chinese leaders.
Any recurrence of activity by the so-called Japanese "ronin" should be strictly and instantly suppressed by the Japanese authorities.
In this connection it is to be noted that the Japanese bluejacket sight-seeing tours in Chapel have been rearranged on a new basis and that the recent Chapel evacuation has accordingly virtually ceased.
That bluejackets were allowed to penetrate into the recent war areas bearing arms was a blunder, but that new arrangements have been made whereby the arms are left behind and the sailors are escorted by Chinese gendarmes is sensible and highly commendable. At least the willingness to face facts and to take action thereon is manifest.

（印：F.I.P.）
（批：36/8/32）

编号 D 3753
30/8/32

及时的一针
社论

大上海市政府正在采取迅速且希望是严厉的措施，以镇压与抵制日货有关的非法和恐怖活动。
吴铁城市长最近与当地商界及其他领袖进行了低调会谈，随后已向日本总领事馆传达了以此为目的的保证。
即使没有立即产生奇迹，这一进展也必须被解读为中方温和与理智的胜利。其他人应以最彻底的坦诚与合作予以回应；这种合作应包括承认那些在逻辑上无法回避的事实。
其中一个事实是，日本继续提供最爱国、最守法的中国人不愿购买日货的理由。吴市长或其他任何中国领袖都无法改变这一局面。
唯一能改变这一局面的力量是日本自己。中国领袖所能做的，就是反对暴力和非法行为，这些行为不仅伤害日本人，而且在各国人民眼中损害了抵制运动本身的事业。
另一个事实是，中国当局的管辖权不延伸至两个租界之内。这一点似乎不言自明，但应认识到，中国“流氓”和勒索者的活动在租界与中国区域之间或多或少相互交织。除非租界妥善整顿内部秩序，否则中国当局的任务将更加艰难。
还应认识到，在上海的日本人对中国同胞及其外籍同胞负有特殊的耐心和不挑衅的义务。他们不在自己的国家；而是在特殊困难的情况下身处他国。因此，应避免一切带有傲慢色彩的行为，特别是鉴于最近在上海和满洲发生的事件。
日本军方、民政和商业领袖采取审慎的政策，可以在很大程度上减轻中国领袖的执法任务。
所谓的日本“浪人”的任何活动复燃，都应受到日本当局的严格和即时镇压。
在这方面，值得注意的是，在闸北（Chapel，原文如此，应为Chapei之误）的日本水兵观光团已在新基础上重新安排，因此最近的闸北撤离实际上已经停止。
允许水兵携带武器进入最近的战区是一个失误，但现已做出新安排，水兵留下武器，由中国宪兵护送，这是明智且值得高度赞扬的。至少，面对事实并采取行动的意愿是显而易见的。

（印：F.I.P.）
（批：36/8/32）

July 30, 1932.
Chen Pao:

THE BOYCOTT OF JAPANESE GOODS.

During the past month, a number of local Chinese merchants have been buying Japanese goods. According to an investigation made by our reporter yesterday, various shops began to stop selling Japanese goods yesterday. The brokers of Japanese goods are trying to change the Japanese trade marks so as to make the goods appear to be Chinese products. Three days ago some $60,000 worth of Japanese cotton cloth, to be sent to Shao Shing, Chekiang, as Chinese goods, was detained at Hangchow.

The Cotton Piece Goods Guild has received 14 letters of warning against dealing in Japanese goods. Among the senders are the following:-
(1) Sulphur Bomb Group.
(2) National Salvation Group.
(3) Special Examination and Investigation Department.
(4) Headquarters.
(5) Bloody Group for the Extermination of Traitors.
(6) Transporters.

Except for the letter sent by the Bloody Group for the Extermination of Traitors, all the other 13 letters were delivered to the Cotton Piece Goods Trade Guild through the post and no address of the senders was given. These letters threaten to shoot or bomb those who do not comply with their demands.

After the new members of the Standing Committee and Supervisory Committee have been elected at to-day's meeting of representatives, the Cotton Piece Goods Trade Guild will persuade its members not to buy Japanese goods anymore.

On July 28, when business transactions started, Mr. Meh Ngur Tse, an important official of the Chinese Cotton Cloth Exchange Brokers' Association took the platform and delivered a speech stating that except for a few undesirable brokers who have secretly sold Japanese goods, no transactions of Japanese goods have taken place in the Exchange and that these undesirable brokers when discovered, would be severely dealt with. As the members of the Brokers' Association have not been dealing in Japanese goods, the Association will not reply to the two letters from the Bloody Group for the Extermination of Traitors.

The Coal Trade Guild will discipline those members who deal in Japanese goods. The Yung Chang Coal Shop, into which a bomb was thrown by the Bloody Group for the Extermination of Traitors, is no longer a full member of the Guild, because it was expelled from the Guild some time ago.

After learning that Yuan Sih Kuen, owner of the Sih Chen Iron Shop, No. 618, North Soochow Road, had bought a large quantity of Japanese iron, the Iron Trade Guild sent a representative to the shop to ascertain whether or not the report was true. It was found that Yuan Sih Kuen had actually bought Japanese iron.

At a meeting held by the Guild, it was decided that the Japanese iron be taken to the Guild to be disposed of as the public desired.

（右上角印章内容：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE & S. B. REGISTRY. No. D 3453/ Date 2/8/32）

1932年7月30日。
《申报》：

抵制日货。

在过去的一个月里，一些本地中国商人一直在购买日货。据本报记者昨日调查，各家店铺于昨日起开始停止销售日货。日货掮客正试图更改日本商标，以使货物看起来像中国产品。三天前，价值约6万美元、拟作为中国货物运往浙江绍兴的日本棉布在杭州被扣留。

棉布业公会已收到14封警告信，要求不得经营日货。发信人包括以下团体：
(1) 硫磺弹团。
(2) 救国团。
(3) 特别审查调查部。
(4) 总部。
(5) 诛奸血团。
(6) 运输队。

除“诛奸血团”发出的信件外，其余13封信均通过邮局送达棉布业同业公会，且未提供发信人地址。这些信件威胁称，将对不遵守其要求者予以枪击或投掷炸弹。

在今日举行的代表会议上选出常务委员会和监察委员会的新成员后，棉布业同业公会将劝告其会员不再购买日货。

7月28日开市时，中国棉布交易所掮客协会的重要官员梅ngur Tse先生（音译）上台发表演讲，称除了少数秘密售卖日货的不良掮客外，交易所内并未发生日货交易，一旦发现此类不良掮客，将予以严厉处置。鉴于掮客协会会员并未经营日货，该协会将不予回复“诛奸血团”的两封来信。

煤炭业同业公会将惩戒那些经营日货的会员。永昌煤号曾被“诛奸血团”投掷炸弹，因其在不久前已被公会除名，故不再是公会的正式会员。

铁业同业公会获悉北苏州路618号四成铁号店主袁Sih Kuen（音译）购买了大量日本铁器后，派代表前往该店核实报道是否属实。经查，袁Sih Kuen确实购买了日本铁器。

在公会召开的会议上，决定将这些日本铁器送至公会，按公众意愿进行处理。

（右上角印章内容：上海公共租界工部局警务处 & S. B. 登记处。编号 D 3453/ 日期 1932年8月2日）
（顶部手写圈注：①）

had been bought from Japanese merchants; he declared
that it had been bought from a broker.
Upon learning the decision of the Guild, Yuan

July 31, 1932.

China Times and other local newspapers:

OPPOSITION TO INCREASE IN TELEPHONE CHARGES.

Representatives from the Special Committees to Oppose
the Increase in Telephone Charges, organised by the Shanghai
Special District Citizens Federation, called at the Shanghai
Municipal Council at 10 a.m. yesterday to submit an appeal for
the cancellation of the increase in telephone charges by the
Shanghai Telephone Company. They were received by Mr. Ho
Tuh Wei, Chinese Associate Secretary.
The callers gave their reasons for opposing the
increase in telephone charges and requested the Council to
draw the attention of the Telephone Company that pending a
settlement of the dispute, the Company should not be allowed
to cut the wires and dismantle the telephones.
Mr. Ho promised to transmit the views of the
delegates to the Council for consideration and suggested that
the Citizens Federation organise a Telephone Subscribers
Federation.
The Special Committee to Oppose the Increase in
Telephone Charges will hold a meeting at 2 p.m. August 2
when a report will be made on the negotiations with the S.M.C.

Chen Pao:

THE BLOODY GROUP FOR THE EXTERMINATION OF TRAITORS.

The Bloody Group for the Extermination of Traitors has
made its presence felt and Chinese merchants are returning goods
to Japanese.
The Group has given out that Lee Chun Sun (李春生)
is the Chief of the Group, Tseu Sz Lo (周士路) is the Chief of
the Executive Department and Ho Bah (何伯) is an ordinary
member of the Group. It is not known whether these are
their real names.

Yesterday the Group sent us a letter stating that
it has not detailed any persons to solicit funds. In its
letter to the Cotton Cloth Exchange, the Group expressed
dissatisfaction with the action of certain members who had
raised the price of Chinese cotton cloth. This shows that
the Group is a genuine patriotic body and it has no other
object but that of helping the nation.

At 5 p.m. yesterday, the Chun Hwa San Te Shop on
Nanking Road, opposite the Continental Emporium, received a
letter from the Group through the post with a bullet enclosed.
The letter warned the shop to stop selling Japanese goods and
to publish an advertisement in the newspapers declaring that
the shop would never deal in Japanese goods any more.
According to Tsang Kee Siang, the manager of the shop,
there are no Japanese goods in his shop.

The Cotton Piece Goods Guild yesterday issued a
declaration emphasising that since the Sino-Korean incident,
the Guild has ceased to deal in Japanese goods.

The Chinese Cotton Cloth Exchange yesterday received
the following letter from the Group through the post:-

日期：1932年8月12日

1932年7月31日。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

反对增加电话费。

由上海特别区市民联合会组织的反对增加电话费特别委员会的代表，于昨日上午10时拜访上海工部局，提交请愿书，要求取消上海电话公司增加电话费的决定。他们受到华籍副秘书何Tuh Wei先生（音译）的接见。
来访者陈述了反对增加电话费的理由，并请求工部局提请电话公司注意，在争议解决之前，不得允许公司切断线路和拆除电话。
何先生承诺将代表的意见转达工部局审议，并建议市民联合会组织一个电话用户联合会。
反对增加电话费特别委员会将于8月2日下午2时举行会议，届时将报告与工部局的谈判情况。

《申报》：

诛奸血团。

诛奸血团已崭露头角，中国商人正在向日方退货。
该团体宣称，李春生是该团团长，周士路是执行部部长，何伯是普通团员。不知这些是否为其真实姓名。

昨日该团体致函本报，称并未派遣任何人募集捐款。在给棉布交易所的信中，该团体对某些会员抬高中国棉布价格的行为表示不满。这表明该团体是一个真正的爱国组织，除了帮助国家外别无其他目的。

昨日下午5时，位于南京路大陆商场对面的春华三德店收到该团体通过邮局寄来的一封信，信中附有一颗子弹。信件警告该店停止销售日货，并在报纸上刊登广告，声明该店永远不再经营日货。据该店经理曾祺祥（音译）称，店内并无日货。

棉布业同业公会昨日发表声明，强调自中韩事件以来，公会已停止经营日货。

中国棉布交易所昨日收到该团体通过邮局寄来的下列信件：
